input.prompt:
Wide establishing shot of a logistics depot's dock exterior at first light. Five bay doors along a concrete apron, two of them open with forklifts idling just inside. A single tractor-trailer is backed up to the third door, its reflective markings catching the low sun. Steam rises faintly from a coffee cup left on a stack of empty pallets in the foreground.

Camera holds a slow, steady push-in over the full fifteen seconds, staying low enough that the dock canopy frames the top of the shot throughout. Cool blue pre-dawn light on the concrete, warming gradually to amber where the sun catches the truck's cab and the edge of the open bay doors as the push-in progresses. Fine mist hangs low over the apron in the first few seconds and thins out by the end of the shot.

No people walking through frame; the lot should feel like the calm just before a shift starts, not empty or abandoned, just quiet. A single security light on the canopy is still lit despite the growing daylight, a small detail that sells the early hour without needing a clock or a sign.

Match the muted, slightly desaturated color grade and gentle film grain of the two attached style references, and keep the motion restrained, almost documentary, rather than sweeping or drone-like. No handheld shake though; this should read as a locked-off or gently motorized push, not a shoulder rig.

Avoid any visible text, logos, or license plates on the trailer; keep signage on the bay doors blank or turned away from camera. Avoid lens flare, avoid a sunrise-in-frame composition, and avoid any birds or wildlife, which tend to render distractingly in this model at this resolution.
